recommendation: Keep this source change. It restores the approved clarification in current core build scope without reintroducing deleted detail pages. A separate follow-up may still be appropriate for the broken external API Incubator async detail links.
issue_request: FHIR-24882 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core change request for the Async page. It asked to extend the async/bulk-data pattern beyond GET/export-style pulls so clients could use an analogous asynchronous pattern for PUT and POST requests, with the approved resolution calling for clarification that async can be used for valid RESTful operations including POST, PUT, and PATCH and for success-result clarity.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-24882 was found. The current source already had a high-level Asynchronous Interaction Request entry from the FHIR-35936 async-page split, and the Jira comment says build.fhir.org/async described that pattern by August 2022. The deleted source/async-bundle.html detail page previously contained the HTTP method, 202 Accepted, and completion Bundle outcome details that satisfied the request.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes record the 2020-03-23 persuasive vote. Zulip discussion documents non-bulk async CRUD use cases including PUT/POST and explains using a Bundle entry to carry final response semantics. Later FHIR-42769 and FHIR-47271 clarified adjacent 202/disambiguation behavior, while the R6 normative cleanup removed the core detail pages and left the current source relying on API Incubator links that currently return 404.
reconciliation: Added a focused paragraph to source/async.html stating that Asynchronous Interaction Request applies to any valid RESTful request the server supports, including create (POST), update (PUT), and patch (PATCH), and that the initial response is 202 Accepted with completion represented by a Bundle first entry carrying the final outcome.
source_changes: source/async.html: added a paragraph under Patterns clarifying POST/PUT/PATCH async interaction applicability, 202 Accepted kick-off response, and completion Bundle outcome semantics.

related_jiras.note: Split and updated the async page family, creating the detail page that previously carried the interaction outcome guidance; already represented on the combined branch.
Clarified 202 Accepted for create by pointing to the Asynchronous Interaction Request pattern, supporting the same completion-status semantics.
Restored _outputFormat disambiguation on the active async overview after the detail pages were removed, adjacent to this reconciliation.
